name: alertops
label: AlertOps
note: AlertOps' v2 API, which reads the key from a header. Version 1 of the same API takes the key as a query parameter instead, and this entry deliberately does not reach it: a credential in a URL is a credential in everybody's logs.

name: axiom
label: Axiom
note: Axiom's management and query API with an API token. Axiom documents api.axiom.co as the address of every endpoint except ingest and query, which go to a region edge host this entry does not cover.

name: betterstack-telemetry
label: Better Stack Telemetry
note: Better Stack's Telemetry API, which is where logs and metrics sources live. Its token is a different one from the Uptime API's, so a key stored here will not reach uptime.betterstack.com.

name: betterstack-uptime
label: Better Stack Uptime
note: Better Stack's Uptime API — monitors, heartbeats, on-call and status pages. The Telemetry side of Better Stack is a separate host and a separate token.

name: checkly
label: Checkly
note: Checkly's public API for synthetic checks and their results. Checkly also documents an X-Checkly-Account header naming the account; this service will not set it, so a key that needs one — a key belonging to somebody in several Checkly accounts — will be refused.

name: cronitor
label: Cronitor
note: Cronitor's monitor API. The key goes in as the HTTP Basic username with no password, which is what Cronitor documents; the telemetry pings a job sends are a different, keyless address and do not pass here.

name: dash0-eu-central-1
label: Dash0 (eu-central-1)
note: Dash0's API in its AWS eu-central-1 deployment. A Dash0 token belongs to one organisation in one region, so a token minted elsewhere will be refused here rather than routed.

name: dash0-eu-west-1
label: Dash0 (eu-west-1)
note: Dash0's API in its AWS eu-west-1 deployment. Pick the region your organisation was created in; a token restricted to particular datasets also needs the dataset named on the call, which the caller supplies.

name: dash0-europe-west4
label: Dash0 (europe-west4)
note: Dash0's API in its Google Cloud europe-west4 deployment, which is a different host from the AWS ones and takes only tokens issued there.

name: dash0-us-west-2
label: Dash0 (us-west-2)
note: Dash0's API in its AWS us-west-2 deployment. Dash0 also accepts the same token as an HTTP Basic password under any username; we send the bearer form its documentation leads with.

name: debugbear
label: DebugBear
note: DebugBear's page-speed monitoring API. A project key reaches one project's results; the project and page endpoints under /projects need the admin key instead, and DebugBear decides which by the key, not by the address.

name: firehydrant
label: FireHydrant
note: FireHydrant's incident API with a bot token. FireHydrant documents the token with the Bearer word, which is what we send; the older bare-Authorization form is not what this entry uses.

name: grafana-cloud
label: Grafana Cloud (account API)
note: The Grafana Cloud account API at grafana.com, with an access policy token: stacks, plugins and access policies. The dashboards and datasources inside a stack are a different host — use the Grafana Cloud stack entry for those.

name: grafana-stack
template_hint: the slug in your stack's address, https://<this>.grafana.net
label: Grafana Cloud (stack)
note: One Grafana Cloud stack's own HTTP API with a service account token — dashboards, datasources, alert rules. The address contains your stack slug, so this entry cannot be probed on our side the way a fixed one can; it was read off Grafana's own service-account page.

name: healthchecks
label: Healthchecks.io
note: The hosted Healthchecks.io management API. Every key is scoped to one project — Healthchecks issues no account-wide key — so one upstream covers one project. A self-hosted instance is a different address entirely.

name: hund
label: Hund
note: Hund's status page API on its shared host. A key with global permissions works as it stands; one scoped to a single status page needs a Hund-Context header naming that page, which this service will not set.

name: ilert
label: ilert
note: ilert's REST API for alerts, on-call schedules and status pages. The inbound events API that monitoring tools post to is a different, per-source address and does not pass through here.

name: incident-io
label: incident.io
note: incident.io's API for incidents, catalog and on-call. One global host: incident.io documents no region-specific address, so there is no EU variant of this entry to choose.

name: instatus
label: Instatus
note: Instatus's API for status pages, components and incidents, behind one bearer key.

name: netdata
label: Netdata Cloud
note: Netdata Cloud's v2 API with a bearer token. Netdata answers these paths to an anonymous caller too, with nothing in them, so a 200 here is not proof the token was accepted — only a token it can read shows real spaces. A token needs scope:all to reach the whole API.

name: newrelic
label: New Relic (US)
note: New Relic's US endpoint — the REST API v2 and NerdGraph — reading a user API key from the Api-Key header. An EU account answers on a different host; use the New Relic (EU) entry for one. A licence or ingest key is not a user key and will be refused.

name: newrelic-eu
label: New Relic (EU)
note: New Relic's EU endpoint, for an account whose data is held in the EU region. A US account's key does not resolve here; the two hosts are separate and New Relic names both.

name: nodeping
label: NodePing
note: NodePing's uptime API. The token goes in as the HTTP Basic username with the password ignored, which NodePing documents; its other two ways of passing it put the token in the URL or the body and are not what we send.

name: ohdear
label: Oh Dear
note: Oh Dear's API for monitors, uptime, broken links and certificate checks, behind one bearer token.

name: pingdom
label: Pingdom
note: Pingdom's API 3.1 for uptime and transaction checks. A read-only Pingdom token is enough for everything this reads and is the safer one to store.

name: rootly
label: Rootly
note: Rootly's incident management API with an API key. Rootly's endpoints expect the JSON:API content type on writes; nothing here sets it for you.

name: sentry
label: Sentry
note: Sentry's web API with an auth token. This is the region-neutral address; an organisation pinned to a data storage location should use the Sentry (US) or Sentry (EU) entry so requests stay in that region.

name: sentry-de
label: Sentry (EU)
note: Sentry's EU region address, which is de.sentry.io — the host Sentry names for an organisation whose data storage location is the European Union. A US organisation's token does not belong here.

name: sentry-us
label: Sentry (US)
note: Sentry's US region address, for an organisation whose data storage location is the United States and which needs its API calls processed there rather than at the region-neutral host.

name: solarwinds-ap01
label: SolarWinds Observability (ap-01)
note: SolarWinds Observability SaaS in its ap-01 data centre. A SolarWinds API token belongs to one data centre, so the wrong entry here sends a live token to a region that will never accept it.

name: solarwinds-eu01
label: SolarWinds Observability (eu-01)
note: SolarWinds Observability SaaS in its eu-01 data centre, for an organisation whose data is held in Europe.

name: solarwinds-na01
label: SolarWinds Observability (na-01)
note: SolarWinds Observability SaaS in its na-01 data centre, which is the North American AWS one and the default for most accounts.

name: solarwinds-na02
label: SolarWinds Observability (na-02)
note: SolarWinds Observability SaaS in its na-02 data centre, which is the North American Azure one. It is a separate tenancy from na-01 and takes only tokens issued there.

name: speedcurve
label: SpeedCurve
note: SpeedCurve's API for sites, tests and page-speed results. The key is the HTTP Basic username and SpeedCurve ignores the password, so we send none.

name: spike
label: Spike.sh
note: Spike.sh's incident and on-call API. Only /teams and /users answer on the key alone; the rest of the API also wants an x-team-id header naming the team, which this service will not set.

name: updown
label: updown.io
note: updown.io's uptime API. The key goes in the header rather than updown's other option of an api-key query parameter, because a credential in a URL ends up in logs we do not control.

name: uptimerobot
label: UptimeRobot
note: UptimeRobot's v3 API, which takes the token as a bearer. The v2 API is a different shape — the key went in the form body and GET was refused — and is not what this entry reaches.
